$comment: Single source of truth for the Windows product identity.
Everything that has to agree - the exe's VERSIONINFO block, the installer,
the Programs & Features entry and the name SmartScreen shows as the
publisher - is stated here once. build_installer.ps1 feeds these values to
Inno Setup, and verify_release.ps1 reads the built binaries back and fails
'publisher' must match the Common Name (CN) of your code signing
certificate. Windows shows the certificate's CN on the SmartScreen and UAC
prompts, and shows this file's value in the file's Properties; if the two
disagree the app looks like it is impersonating someone.
description: Send files across your local network, with no internet
$comment_appId: Never change: it is what lets a new version upgrade the old one in place.
$comment_timestamp: RFC 3161 timestamp servers, tried in order. A timestamp is what keeps a
signature valid after the certificate expires - without one every release
goes unsigned the day the certificate lapses, and its reputation with it.
$comment_legacy: What the exe's VERSIONINFO said before this release. path_provider on
fields, so correcting them moves where shared_preferences lives. The
installer copies the old file across once so nobody loses their device
name, theme or history. Safe to delete once no com.example build is left.
